scenes.headline: How a pruned matrix product broke 3SUM and APSP
scenes.sub: Alman and Vassilevska Williams, from an algorithm Claude found.
scenes.say: Hi, I'm Trio! Two problems everyone assumed were stuck at textbook speed just got faster.

scenes.text: Compute only the wanted entries of a thin matrix product, by visiting only the recursion leaves those entries need.
scenes.say: Compute just the entries you want from a thin matrix product, and touch only the recursion they need.

steps.say: Both problems reduce to one question. Does a weighted graph have a triangle whose weights add to zero?
Hash the weights modulo a small prime, and that becomes triangle checks in lopsided graphs.
Each check is a few entries of a long, thin matrix product. Speed that up, and everything above speeds up.

scenes.title: Schönhage's identity, recursed
scenes.say: The engine is an old identity.

items.say: Ten multiplications compute a three by three outer product and an inner product at once.
Applied level after level, one run multiplies many thin matrices.
The sums that prepare each leaf are computed once and shared.
Then a branch is entered only if a wanted entry needs it.

parts.note: leaves of order d in one tile
parts.say: Leaves shared by many entries get rarer as their order grows.
Their total at least halves with every step, so they cost almost nothing.

parts.note: a deep recursion makes it so
parts.say: That needs a very deep recursion, which is why the matrices must be astronomically large.

scenes.label: deterministic 3SUM, below the textbook n squared
scenes.say: The result: three sum in n to the one point nine nine nine two, and shortest paths just under n cubed.

scenes.label: inputs needed before the exponent alone makes 3SUM 2x faster
scenes.say: It is not practical. On the exponent alone, inputs need hundreds of digits in their size before it is twice as fast.

scenes.text: Reductions built to prove hardness are also algorithms: one fast routine at the bottom speeds up everything above it.
scenes.say: Reductions built to prove hardness are also algorithms. One fast routine sped up dozens of problems.

recap: 3SUM and APSP reduce to thin products
Prune the recursion to wanted leaves
Galactic, but the hypotheses are gone
scenes.say: Thin products at the bottom, pruned recursion inside, and two hypotheses gone.
